quiz.question: By what date must a federally regulated bank submit its annual harassment and violence report?
options: On or before 31 January each year
Within 90 days after the bank's fiscal year end
On or before 30 June each year
On or before 1 March each year
quiz.explanation: Section 36 requires the annual report to the Head of Compliance and Enforcement on or before 1 March, covering occurrences notified in the previous calendar year.

quiz.question: What period does the annual report cover?
options: Occurrences notified in the previous calendar year
Occurrences in the bank's last fiscal year
Only occurrences that went to investigation
Every occurrence since 2021
quiz.explanation: The report covers occurrences for which notice was given in the preceding calendar year, regardless of how they were resolved.

quiz.question: Which information does the annual report ask for?
options: The names of all responding parties
Copies of every investigator's report, with the names of the parties removed by the employer first
The number of sexual and non-sexual occurrences and the average time to resolve them
Each employee's training certificate
quiz.explanation: The report gives aggregate figures: totals, sexual and non-sexual split, deaths, grounds if known, locations, relationships, how processes ended and the average time. It contains no names.

quiz.question: An occurrence at a branch results in an employee's death. When must the bank report it to the Head of Compliance and Enforcement?
options: Within seven days
Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the death
In the next annual report
Within 30 days, after its own investigation
quiz.explanation: Section 37 requires a fatality report within 24 hours after the employer becomes aware of the employee's death.

quiz.question: How long must the bank keep a record of each notice of an occurrence and the actions taken?
options: Two years
Five years
Ten years
Seven years
quiz.explanation: Section 35(1)(e) lists notices and actions taken, and section 35(2) requires those records to be kept for ten years.

quiz.question: What is the maximum administrative monetary penalty per violation under Part IV of the Code?
quiz.explanation: The Code caps a Part IV penalty at CAD 250,000 per violation; the amount depends on the type of violation, the size of the business and previous penalties.

quiz.question: What did several employers on the Labour Program's April 2026 list receive CAD 500 penalties for?
options: Not submitting the annual harassment and violence occurrence report for 2024
Failing to train employees within three months
Failing to appoint a designated recipient
Refusing to cooperate with an investigator
quiz.explanation: The public naming page listed CAD 500 penalties for failing to submit the Employer's Annual Harassment and Violence Occurrence Report for reporting year 2024.

quiz.question: Why is the Equitable Bank listing relevant to a harassment prevention programme, even though it concerned Part III?
options: It was the first time the Labour Program penalised a bank for failing to prevent workplace harassment
It shows banks are enforced against and named under the same Code and penalty system
It shows OSFI enforces the Canada Labour Code
It proves Part II does not apply to banks
quiz.explanation: The penalties were for labour standards breaches, not harassment, but they show a federally regulated bank being penalised and named under Part IV of the Code, which also backs Part II.

quiz.question: The employer and policy committee disagreed on an assessment update and the employer decided. What must the employer keep?
options: Nothing, because the employer's decision prevails
Minutes signed by every committee member
A ruling from the Labour Program
A record of its decision and the reasons for it
quiz.explanation: Section 35(1)(d) requires a record of the employer's decision and reasons for each joint matter where agreement failed, and it is kept for ten years.

quiz.question: Which task belongs to every employee rather than to management or committees?
options: Submitting the annual report to the Labour Program
Choosing the investigator from the joint list and deciding which of the report's recommendations to adopt
Completing harassment prevention training and reporting hazards or suspected breaches
Reviewing the prevention policy every three years
quiz.explanation: Employees must report hazards and suspected breaches under section 126 and receive training; the employer files reports and, with committees, maintains the policy and process.

bank.question: A foreign bank operating in Canada through an authorized branch asks whether the Canada Labour Code's harassment rules apply to its Toronto staff. What is the best answer?
options: No: only Canadian-incorporated banks are covered
Only if the head office is in Canada
Yes: an authorized foreign bank is a federal undertaking, so Part II applies
Only if OSFI adopts the rules in a guideline
bank.explanation: The Code's list of federal works, undertakings and businesses includes a bank or an authorized foreign bank within the meaning of the Bank Act. OSFI does not need to adopt the Labour Code.

bank.question: A trader posts repeated 'jokes' about a colleague's religion in a desk chat. He says he meant no harm. How does Part II treat this?
options: It can be, because the test is what could reasonably be expected to cause offence or harm
It is not harassment and violence, because he did not intend harm and said so as soon as he was asked
It is only a human rights issue, outside Part II
It counts only if the colleague complains in writing
bank.explanation: The Code's definition turns on conduct that can reasonably be expected to cause offence, humiliation or injury, not intent. It may also engage the Canadian Human Rights Act, but that does not take it outside Part II; notice can be oral.

bank.question: Which statement correctly describes the purpose of Part II of the Code?
options: To set minimum wages, hours of work, holiday pay and termination notice for federally regulated employees
To regulate collective bargaining between banks and unions
To set capital requirements for federally regulated banks
To prevent accidents, harassment and violence, and work-related physical or psychological harm
bank.explanation: Section 122.1 states Part II's purpose as preventing accidents, occurrences of harassment and violence and physical or psychological injuries and illnesses. Wages are Part III and collective bargaining is Part I.

bank.question: Granite Bay's head of HR says: 'We train employees, so the executive team doesn't need the harassment course.' Which provision contradicts this?
options: Paragraph 125(1)(z.17), on posting committee members' names
Paragraph 125(1)(z.162), which requires the employer itself to undergo the training
Section 128, on refusing dangerous work
Subsection 125(4), on former employees
bank.explanation: Paragraph (z.162) requires the employer to undergo harassment and violence prevention training, and the Regulations require the employer to be trained at least every three years.

bank.question: The bank appoints a new person to receive harassment complaints. Which requirement does paragraph 125(1)(z.163) set for that person?
options: At least ten years of service at the bank and membership of the policy health and safety committee
Knowledge, training and experience in harassment and violence issues and knowledge of relevant legislation
Membership of the policy health and safety committee
A law degree and bar admission
bank.explanation: Paragraph (z.163) requires the person designated to receive complaints to have knowledge, training and experience in harassment and violence issues and knowledge of the relevant laws. It does not require a law degree or committee membership.

bank.question: A Granite Bay rural branch normally employs 12 people and no committee is required there. What must the bank do for that work place?
options: Nothing, because it is too small
Set up a full work place committee anyway
Appoint a health and safety representative selected by the non-managerial employees
Let the branch manager act as both employer and representative
bank.explanation: Section 136 requires a representative for each work place with fewer than 20 employees normally employed, or where no committee is required, selected by employees who do not exercise managerial functions.

bank.question: An employee reasonably believes a branch's broken security door creates a danger to her during closing. Which right does Part II give her?
options: A right to refuse to work in that place, subject to the Code's conditions and process
A right to close the branch permanently and move its staff to the nearest branch until a new door is fitted
A right to call OSFI to inspect the branch
No right, because banks are low-risk work places
bank.explanation: Section 128 lets an employee refuse to work in a place or perform an activity if they have reasonable cause to believe it is a danger, subject to the Code's limits and procedure.

bank.question: After an employee reported a hazard, her manager moved her to a less desirable shift 'to keep things calm'. Which conclusion is best?
options: This is acceptable because shift changes are a management right
This is acceptable if the hazard report was later found to be minor
This is only a concern if she is a committee member
This may be a prohibited reprisal under section 147 because it penalises her for acting under Part II
bank.explanation: Section 147 bars employers from imposing financial or other penalties or disciplinary action on an employee for acting under Part II or giving information about health and safety conditions.

bank.question: Granite Bay has no policy committee for a separately incorporated subsidiary with 150 employees in one office. Who is the applicable partner there?
options: The parent bank's policy committee automatically
The designated recipient
The Labour Program
The work place committee for that office
bank.explanation: The applicable partner is the policy committee or, if there is none, the work place committee or the health and safety representative. A 150-person work place has a work place committee.

bank.question: Which pair of risk factors must the joint work place assessment consider under section 8?
options: Employees' credit scores and criminal records, as gathered through the bank's background check process
The physical design of the work place and existing psychological health and safety measures
The bank's lending targets and interest rates
Customer satisfaction ratings and complaint volumes
bank.explanation: Section 8 lists culture, conditions, activities and structure; external circumstances such as family violence; reports and data; physical design; and measures protecting psychological health and safety.

bank.question: The assessment identified risk factors on 1 April. The committee proposes to implement preventive measures 'by the end of next year'. What is the problem?
options: Measures must be developed, planned and implemented within six months of identifying the risks
There is no problem, because the Regulations set no deadline for preventive measures after the assessment
The deadline is three months, not six
Only OSFI can set the deadline
bank.explanation: Section 9 requires the measures, an implementation plan and implementation within six months after the risk factors are identified.

bank.question: A preventive measure proposed for a branch, such as moving a lone employee to an isolated back office, would reduce one risk but create another. What do the Regulations require of measures?
options: Any measure is acceptable if it reduces at least one risk
Measures are optional suggestions for the employer
To the extent feasible, they mitigate risk and neither create nor increase risk
Measures need only be approved by the branch manager
bank.explanation: Section 9 requires preventive measures that, as far as feasible, mitigate the risk of harassment and violence and do not create or increase it.

bank.question: Which of these is NOT among the elements the prevention policy must contain?
options: A description of the support measures available
A summary of the emergency procedures
The names of employees who gave notice in the past year
How privacy of people involved will be protected
bank.explanation: The policy must include support measures, emergency procedures and privacy protections, among others. Naming people who gave notice would be the opposite of what the policy's privacy element requires.

bank.question: The bank changes who acts as its designated recipient. What does this mean for the prevention policy?
options: Nothing until the three-year review
The policy must be resubmitted to the Labour Program for approval
Only the intranet page needs updating
The policy must be jointly reviewed and updated, because one of its elements changed
bank.explanation: Section 10(4) requires a joint review and, if necessary, update at least every three years and after any change to an element of the policy, which includes the designated recipient's name or identity.

bank.question: An employee has been at Granite Bay for three years and two months and last completed the harassment training in her first month. Is she compliant?
options: Yes: a single session at hiring is enough, and refreshers are only good practice that the bank may choose
No: training is required at least once every three years after the first session
Yes: refreshers are needed only for managers
No: training is required every year
bank.explanation: Section 12(4)(b) requires training at least once every three years after the initial training. Annual training is not required by the Regulations, though a bank may choose it.

bank.question: The policy committee updates the training to cover a new remote-work risk. What follows for existing employees?
options: They must receive the updated training, since training follows any update
Nothing until each person's three-year refresher
Only new hires receive the updated course
Only managers must take the new content
bank.explanation: Section 12(4)(c) requires training following any update to the training under subsection (3), as well as after assignment to a riskier role.

bank.question: Granite Bay's harassment training explains the policy and how to recognise and respond to harassment, but says nothing about the Canadian Human Rights Act. What is missing?
options: The required link between harassment and violence and the prohibited grounds of discrimination
Nothing, since human rights law is a separate subject
The bank's anti-bribery rules and gifts policy, which the Regulations require in every harassment course
The bank's capital adequacy ratios
bank.explanation: Section 12(2)(b) requires the training to describe the relationship between work place harassment and violence and the prohibited grounds of discrimination in subsection 3(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act.

bank.question: A notice of an occurrence must include certain information. Which set is correct?
options: Only the responding party's name, job title, branch and the name of their direct manager at the time
A signed statement from two witnesses
A medical certificate and the date
The names of the principal and responding parties if known, the date, and a detailed description
bank.explanation: Section 16 requires the parties' names if known, the date of the occurrence and a detailed description. Witness statements and medical certificates are not required.

bank.question: An anonymous notice describes harassment but gives no way of identifying who was targeted. What happens after the initial review?
options: An investigation must start immediately
The notice must be forwarded to the police
The occurrence is deemed resolved, though the information can still inform prevention
The bank must email all staff to find the person
bank.explanation: Section 19(2) deems the occurrence resolved if the notice does not name or otherwise identify the principal party. The bank can still use the information in its assessment.

bank.question: The CEO is named as the responding party in a notice. Where must that notice go?
options: To the CEO's executive assistant
To the designated recipient
To the chair of the audit committee
To OSFI
bank.explanation: Section 15(3) requires notice to be given to the designated recipient when the employer is the principal or responding party. This avoids the employer handling a notice about itself.

bank.question: Notice was given on 1 June. The employer has not started any effort to resolve the occurrence by 20 July. Which rule has been missed?
options: The investigation must start within 30 days
Reasonable efforts to resolve must begin no later than 45 days after notice
The process must finish within 30 days
Nothing, because no time limit applies
bank.explanation: Section 23(1) requires reasonable efforts to resolve to begin no later than 45 days after notice. From 1 June, that limit passed in mid-July.

bank.question: During negotiated resolution, the principal party and the designated recipient jointly agree that the notice does not describe harassment and violence. What is the effect?
options: The responding party must still be disciplined
An investigation must still take place
That joint determination can resolve the occurrence
The notice must be reported to the Labour Program
bank.explanation: Section 23(3) says resolution includes a joint determination by the principal party and the employer or designated recipient that the notice does not describe harassment and violence.

bank.question: Granite Bay has no joint list of investigators, and the parties cannot agree on one within 60 days of the notice of investigation. Who is chosen?
options: The head of HR, who becomes the investigator by default whenever the parties fail to agree on one
A person chosen by the responding party
An investigator appointed by OSFI
A person identified by the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety as qualified
bank.explanation: Section 27 says that without a joint list, the investigator is someone the parties agree on or, failing agreement within 60 days, one of those the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety identifies.

bank.question: An investigation is under way when the principal and responding parties settle the matter through conciliation. What happens to the investigation?
options: It must be discontinued if the matter is resolved before the report is provided
It must continue to a final report
It is paused for up to one year in case the settlement breaks down, then resumes where it stopped
It continues, but its report stays secret
bank.explanation: Section 25(2) requires the investigation to be discontinued if the occurrence is resolved by negotiated resolution or conciliation before the investigator provides the report.

bank.question: A work place committee asks the designated recipient for the names of the parties in an investigation so it can 'understand the pattern'. What should happen?
options: The names must be shared because the committee is a joint partner
The names can be shared if the CEO approves
The names must be posted in the committee minutes
The committee should not receive identifying information without the person's consent
bank.explanation: Section 135.11 of the Code bars giving a committee information likely to reveal the identity of a person involved in an occurrence without consent. Investigator reports also must not identify people.

bank.question: A principal party ends the resolution process before the occurrence is resolved. What does this trigger for the work place assessment?
options: A joint review, and update if needed, that takes the circumstances of the occurrence into account
Approval of the closure by the Labour Program
A new assessment chosen by the responding party
Nothing until the next three-year review
bank.explanation: Section 6 requires a joint review and, if needed, update of the assessment when an occurrence is not resolved and the principal party ends the process, or when the responding party is neither an employee nor the employer.

bank.question: Which OSFI publication sets expectations for codes of conduct, background checks on all employees and contractors, and reporting of foreign interference?
options: Guideline B-13 Technology and Cyber Risk Management
Guideline E-21 Operational Risk Management and Resilience
The Integrity and Security Guideline
The Work Place Harassment and Violence Prevention Regulations
bank.explanation: The Integrity and Security Guideline (January 2024) covers integrity (character, culture, governance, compliance) and security (premises, people, technology, data, third parties and threat reporting).

bank.question: A Granite Bay credit officer's spouse becomes a director of a borrower she manages. What does OSFI's guideline expect of the bank's code of conduct here?
options: It should ignore family links that arise outside working hours, because they are private matters for the officer
It should cover how real, potential and perceived conflicts are detected, disclosed, avoided and managed
It should leave the decision entirely to the officer
It should require OSFI's approval before she continues
bank.explanation: OSFI expects codes to cover the detection, disclosure, avoidance and management of real, potential and perceived conflicts of interest, with conformity monitored based on risk.

bank.question: Granite Bay's code of conduct was last reviewed in 2019 and nobody tracks whether staff follow it. Which OSFI expectations are not being met?
options: Codes only need to be signed once at hiring, so the bank's current approach already meets OSFI's expectations
Codes are reviewed only when OSFI asks
Codes should be assessed for effectiveness, reviewed regularly, and conformity monitored based on risk
Monitoring is required only for the board
bank.explanation: OSFI expects codes of conduct to be assessed for effectiveness, reviewed and updated regularly, and conformity monitored based on risk, considering roles and exposure to undue influence.

bank.question: A long-serving employee with a clean check at hiring is moving into a role with access to the bank's most sensitive client data. What does OSFI's guideline suggest?
options: Nothing, because her original check remains valid
An off-cycle review of her background check under the bank's criteria for higher-risk roles
Immediate dismissal until a new check is done
Only a new reference from her current manager
bank.explanation: OSFI expects checks to be renewed regularly and reviewed off-cycle based on set criteria, with standards considering authority, seniority and access to sensitive information.

bank.question: Which OSFI expectation in the Corporate Governance Guideline relates most directly to culture and integrity?
options: The board and senior management should promote a risk culture that stresses integrity and effective risk management
The CEO should also chair the board, so that one leader sets a single clear tone on culture across the bank
Oversight functions should report to business line heads
The chief risk officer's pay should be tied to business line revenue
bank.explanation: OSFI expects the board and senior management to promote a risk culture stressing integrity. It views separating the Chair and CEO as critical, wants oversight functions independent, and says the CRO's pay should not be tied to business line performance.

bank.question: What does Guideline E-17 expect each federally regulated bank to have?
options: A public register of every employee's criminal record
Annual OSFI interviews of all branch managers
A ban on hiring directors from other banks
A written policy for assessing the suitability and integrity of its directors and senior management
bank.explanation: E-17 expects a written Assessment Policy, approved by senior management, on assessing the suitability and integrity of Responsible Persons such as directors and senior management.

bank.question: A procurement analyst suspects that a bidder linked to a foreign state is pressuring colleagues to share building access plans. What should the bank's process do?
options: Investigate promptly and confidentially, consider telling CSIS or the RCMP, and inform OSFI of any report
Ignore it unless money has been lost
Confront the bidder publicly at the next procurement meeting so that other suppliers are deterred from trying
Wait for the next annual threat assessment
bank.explanation: Principle 10 expects prompt detection and careful, confidential investigation of suspected undue influence or foreign interference, encourages reporting to authorities such as CSIS and the RCMP, and expects OSFI to be informed immediately.

bank.question: How often does OSFI expect the threat environment, including threats linked to third parties, to be assessed and reported internally?
options: Every five years
Only after a security breach
Only when OSFI requests it
At least annually
bank.explanation: The Integrity and Security Guideline expects the threat environment, including as it relates to third parties, to be assessed and internally reported at least annually.

bank.question: The bank's records manager wants to delete harassment investigation files after seven years, in line with a general retention schedule. What is the issue?
options: None: seven years is the legal minimum for all employment records, so the general schedule can be followed
The Regulations require investigators' reports and related records to be kept for ten years
Files must be kept permanently
Files must be sent to the Labour Program after seven years
bank.explanation: Section 35(2) requires the records in paragraphs (1)(c) to (i), including investigators' reports and notice records, to be kept for ten years.

bank.question: Which item does the annual occurrence report have to include, if known?
options: The names of all principal parties
Each investigator's fee
The number of occurrences linked to each prohibited ground of discrimination
A copy of the prevention policy
bank.explanation: Section 36 asks, if known, for the number of occurrences under each prohibited ground in the Canadian Human Rights Act, alongside other aggregate figures. No names are included.

bank.question: Which factors does the Labour Program use to set the amount of an administrative monetary penalty?
options: The employer's share price and profit
The type of violation, the size of the business and any previous penalties
The number of media reports about the employer
Only the number of employees affected
bank.explanation: The Labour Program explained that penalties are calculated by the type of violation, the size of the business and previous penalties for violations of the same or higher classification, up to CAD 250,000.

bank.question: Why does the Labour Program publish the names of employers who receive penalties?
options: To replace penalties with public warnings, so that employers who are named do not have to pay anything
To let OSFI adjust banks' capital requirements
To encourage compliance, since employers value their reputation, and to inform workers
To identify the employees who were harmed
bank.explanation: The public naming page explains that naming encourages compliance to protect reputation and raises awareness among current and potential employees.

bank.question: An occurrence was not resolved within one year and no party was absent. What must the bank have on file?
options: A Labour Program extension certificate
Written consent from the responding party
A board resolution approving the delay
A document setting out the reason for the delay
bank.explanation: Section 35(1)(f) requires a document giving the reason whenever a time limit in section 33 is not met. The Regulations do not provide for an extension certificate.

bank.question: Granite Bay's chief human resources officer asks which body enforces the harassment and violence rules for the bank. What is the correct answer?
options: The Labour Program of Employment and Social Development Canada
OSFI
The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Each provincial workers' compensation board
bank.explanation: The Labour Program enforces Part II of the Code for federally regulated employers, including banks. OSFI is the prudential supervisor; FCAC supervises consumer conduct.

bank.question: A Labour Program official asks Granite Bay to show it meets the harassment training timetable. Which evidence answers that question best?
options: A copy of the vendor's invoice and licence agreement for the e-learning course used across the bank
The prevention policy's mission statement
Each person's start date, first training date, refreshers and retraining after updates or role changes
The number of employees who opened the intranet page
bank.explanation: The timetable in section 12 is per person: within three months of starting, at least every three years, and after updates or riskier roles. Only person-level dates show that; an invoice or page views do not.

bank.question: An assessor asks how Granite Bay's two frameworks connect: the Labour Code harassment programme and OSFI's integrity expectations. Which answer is strongest?
options: They are unrelated regimes, so they should be run by separate teams that never share information or reports
Both need clear policies, regular training, safe speak-up channels, reprisal protection and reporting to leaders
OSFI's guideline replaces the Labour Code for banks
The Labour Code applies only to branches and OSFI only to head office
bank.explanation: The two regimes have different legal bases and enforcers, but both expect written policies, training, channels to raise concerns, protection for those who speak up and reporting to leadership. Neither replaces the other.
